House Bill 449 (COMMITTEE SUBSTITUTE) By: Representatives Rhodes of The Senate Committee on Regulated Industries and Utilities offered the 124th, Ridley of the 6th, Hitchens of the 161st, Smith of the 70th, Williams of the 148th, and others following substitute to HB 449: MOOT
A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT
To amend Title Titles 44 and 46 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to property and public utilities and public transportation, respectively, so as to subject prohibit certain restrictions on the rates and charges installation, operation, or maintenance of private water wells for irrigation purposes on real property; to prohibit covenants running with the land from prohibiting or restricting property owners from installing, operating, or maintaining private water wells for irrigation purposes on their property; to prohibit companies that provide water services provided through certain water systems in this state to regulation by the Public Service Commission; from prohibiting or restricting customers of such company from installing, operating, or maintaining private water wells for irrigation purposes on such customers' property; to provide for the review of certain increases to such rates and charges by the commission; to provide for financial record keeping of companies that own such water systems; to provide for rules and regulations; to provide for assessments and legislative recommendations by the commission; to provide for statutory construction; to provide for definitions; to provide an effective date; to provide for related matters; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.
BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF GEORGIA:
SECTION 1. Title 44 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to property, is amended in Article 3 of Chapter 5, relating to covenants and warranties, by adding a new Code section to read as follows: "44-5-60.1. (a) No covenant running with the land shall prohibit or restrict a property owner from installing, operating, or maintaining a water well on such property owner's property that exclusively provides water for irrigation purposes to such property, provided that such water well does not provide water to any other parcel of land that is not owned by such property owner and such property owner does not sell water from such water well or, in exchange for consideration, authorize the use of such water well by any other person. (b) Any provision in a covenant running with the land, or any subsidiary document adopted pursuant to a covenant running with the land, that violates subsection (a) of this Code section is declared to be contrary to public policy and shall be void and unenforceable. (c) It is the intent of the General Assembly that the provisions of this Code section shall apply to any covenant running with the land, or any subsidiary document adopted pursuant to a covenant running with the land, regardless of when such covenant running with the land was created or became effective. (d) Nothing in this Code section is intended to prevent the application of any provision of law or regulation of any county, municipality, or consolidated government concerning the installation, operation, or maintenance of water wells in this state." SECTION 2. Title 46 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to public utilities and public transportation, is amended by revising Chapter 10, which is reserved, as follows:
"CHAPTER 10
46-10-1. As used in this chapter, the term: (1) 'Covered water system' means any water system that is owned and operated by a private company and that provides water services by means of pipes or conduits to 2,000 or more customer service connections in this state. Such term … facilities under the control of the operator of such system and used primarily in connection with such system and any collection or pretreatment storage facilities not under such control which are used primarily in connection with such system.
46-10-2. The rates and charges for water services provided through covered water systems shall be just and reasonable and shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the commission as provided in Code Section 46-10-3. 46-10-3. (a) Any increase to the rates or charges for water services provided through a covered water system that would amount to an increase of 15 percent or more to the lowest amount such rates or charges have been set over the prior three calendar years shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the commission as provided in Code Section 46-2-25, including, without limitation, the authority of the commission, upon its election, to enter upon a hearing concerning the lawfulness of such increase, and the company that owns such covered water system shall comply with the notice provisions of subsection (a) of said Code section prior to making such increase to such rates or charges. (b) If a hearing on the lawfulness of an increase to the rates or charges for water services provided through a covered water system is held pursuant to subsection (a) of this Code section and the commission determines at such hearing that such increase is just and reasonable, the commission shall not hold another hearing concerning an increase to the rates or charges for water services provided through such covered water system for a period of three years, unless the company that owns such covered water system intends to increase the rates or charges for such water services during such three-year period by 15 percent or more to the rates or charges found to be just and reasonable by the commission at such hearing. (c) For purposes of calculating whether an increase to the rates or charges for water services provided through a covered water system constitutes an increase of 15 percent or more to the lowest amount such rates or charges have been set over the prior three calendar years, the following shall not be included in such calculation: (1) One-time fees or charges assessed by the company that owns such covered water system for connecting to the water or sewer lines of such covered water system; or (2) Recovered costs that were incurred by the company that owns such covered water system as the result of a flood, tornado, hurricane, earthquake, or other occurrence for which the President of the United States has made a federal disaster declaration under the federal Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act, 42 U.S.C. Sections 5121-5206. 46-10-4.
